cues.en: You also need to be clear on where the boundaries of separation are and when you cross that line. cues.zh: 你还需要清楚分隔的边界在哪里，以及什么时候越过了这条线。我见过很多结构很糟糕的列表程序，到处都在用 eval，其实完全没必要，只是觉得这样方便。问题在于，它以难以预测的方式跨越了语言和元语言之间的界限，让程序更难理解。

cues.en: A lot of languages is about... Language is about naming things, talking about things, and you have to manage those names. And if you don't plan for an appropriate

cues.zh: 命名空间管理机制，随着语言的发展，局面就会失控。做一个小型脚本语言很容易，比如直接定下“所有变量都是全局的”。但随后你就会发现，

cues.en: well, two different guys wanna use I for their do loop and you're gonna run into problems. And and it happens at all levels.

cues.en: It's important to allow name reuse because name reuse is one of the principal supports of brevity which Paul has already addressed. If you make... If you're... Impose a requirement that every name be unique, then you're going to have an unmanageably clumsy language. And if you're going to be able to use renames you need to do it in a disciplined way hence namespace control.
cues.zh: 允许重用名称很重要，因为重用名称是简洁表达的重要支撑之一，保罗已经谈到过这一点。如果你要求每个名称都必须唯一，语言就会变得笨拙得难以使用。而要支持重命名，就需要有条理地管理，这就是命名空间控制的作用。

cues.en: I've got a couple of complaints about how Java did this. It turns out Java has access keywords such as private and public and protected.

cues.en: Turns out protected has a very strange edge case where you where you three classes a, b, c. C inherits from b, b inherits from a.
cues.zh: 结果发现，protected 有个很奇怪的边界情况：有三个类 a、b、c，c 继承自 b，b 继承自 a。

cues.en: B is in a different package but c is in the same package as a and some very strange things happen to the rules there. The access control is not well defined in that case.
cues.zh: B 属于不同的包，但 c 和 a 在同一个包里，那里的规则就会变得非常奇怪。在这种情况下，访问控制并没有被很好地定义。

cues.en: Java subclassing is very strange. If you give
cues.zh: Java 的子类化机制非常奇怪。如果你赋予

cues.en: another program entity the right to declare a variable of a class, you have given that entity the ability to define a subclass of a class.

cues.zh: 这把编译器害惨了。要知道，如果编译器能确定“这个类只有五个子类，且不会再有更多了”，那就太理想了。
